We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts: 139.25, 134.60, 129.00, 129.00, 128.30, 128.30, 49.40, 26.10, 11.40 ppm.

We need number of CH3 groups in the compound. Methyl carbon typically appears around 10-15 ppm for aliphatic CH3 attached to carbon (e.g., methyl of alkane). Also 20-30 ppm for CH3 attached to heteroatoms or aromatic? 26.10 could be CH3 attached to something else (maybe isopropyl). 11.40 is typical for a terminal methyl (e.g., CH3-CH2-). 49.40 could be a carbon attached to heteroatom (e.g., O-CH3). But we need count of CH3 groups. Each CH3 carbon appears as a distinct signal. We have signals at 11.40 (likely CH3), 26.10 (maybe CH3), 49.40 (maybe CH3 attached to O? O-CH3 appears ~55 ppm). 49.4 could be a CH2? Actually CH2 attached to aromatic maybe ~35-45. But CH3 attached to heteroatom (OCH3) ~55. So 49.4 maybe a CH2. So likely two methyl groups: 11.40 and 26.10. Need confirm with proton NMR maybe. Let's get proton NMR.
